newsitem.title: USA: Ascend offers to tame Internet congestion. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Ascend offers to tame Internet congestion. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]

text.p: Ascend Communications Inc said Monday it is now offering a series of high performance Internet Protocol (IP) switches designed to solve congestion problems on telephone carrier and Internet backbones.

In a statement, the company said the series' initial product, the GRF 400, "is the only true IP switch on the market" to offer customers a choice of high-speed transmission media, including ATM and SONET.
Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) and Synchronous Optical Network (SONET) are two methods for transmitting voice and data at high speeds over broadband communications networks.
Available for immediate order, prices for the GRF 400 start at $15,650, including software, the company said.

It said the GRF can forward information based on Internet Protocols at unprecedented speeds -- up to 2.8 million packets per second -- a capacity not available in network backbones built with conventional routers or other switches.
The company said the GRF 400 is an IP switch designed to replace conventional routers and edge switches.
Edge switches refer to equipment located at the edge of the core backbone networks -- in other words equipment that connects the network backbone to individual customer premises.

Ascend (corrects company name) said the architecture of the GRF reduces the number of wide area switches currently now required in networks. Functions once handled by edge switches can be handled in the backbone of the network using these products.
The GRF 400 is the first product to be introduced by Ascend's recently formed High Performance Networking Division (formerly NetStar Inc), based in Minneapolis.

"The Internet congestion problem, as a result of router processing power limitations and bandwidth bottlenecks, has become a major stumbling block as the amount of Internet traffic continues to increase," said Liza Henderson, a consultant with TeleChoice Inc, a telecoms consulting firm.
"Thankfully, router vendors are making significant development strides in software and now in hardware, with Ascend's GRF 400 IP switch, in attempts to minimize and alleviate these concerns."
Ascend stock was among the most active issues on Nasdaq, up two points to 60 in mid-morning trading Monday.
